title: What an AI employee really costs per hour
description: The tokens cost tens of dollars a month. The monthly fee is the visible part. The number that decides it is the time your team spends checking the work.
answer: A managed digital employee costs £5,000 a month, or £60,000 a year, at October 2026 prices. Spread across the hours it covers and the work it carries at once, that is about £1.60 an hour. The software is cheap. Your staff time is not.

sections.h: The software is the cheap part
p: Google's Gemini 4 Argon went live on 14 October 2026 at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. A token is about three quarters of a word, so a million tokens is roughly 750,000 words. A long customer enquiry, with the customer's history attached, runs to a few thousand input tokens. Hundreds of those in a month land in the tens of dollars.

That is the number people use to argue AI is nearly free. True, and almost useless. A month of usage for a five person business costs about what a team lunch costs. It tells you nothing about whether the work gets done.

sections.h: The fee is the part you sign
p: At £5,000 a month, a managed digital employee costs £60,000 a year and runs all 8,760 hours of it. That is about £6.85 an hour of cover, nights and weekends included. Count the several things it can carry at once, an enquiry answered while an invoice is chased, and the cost per hour worked falls to roughly £1.60.

The National Living Wage in October 2026 is £13.20 an hour. However you do the sum, that gap is what this article sits inside. And the fee is not padding. Connecting your email, diary, CRM and accounting, then teaching it what may be promised and who gets told, takes skills most small firms do not have on the payroll.

The American Express SME Business Barometer in July 2026 found UK small business owners and staff spend an estimated 11 hours a week on admin and finance. Eleven hours is a working day and a half, every week, forever.

In a small business that work is nobody's job and everybody's second job. The owner does it at ten at night. The office manager does it between everything else. Set the three person cost below against £60,000 a year and the lazy reading says the human is cheaper. It fails one check: those hours are duplicated across the team, and the software does not care whether it is Tuesday or three in the morning.

sections.h: The cost that sinks the sum
p: Now the line most comparisons skip: checking. If a person has to approve every action before it counts, nothing has been removed. The work has been rearranged into a harder shape, because checking a stranger's work against your own memory of what is true is harder than doing it yourself.

So draw the line yourself. Anything that cannot hurt anyone if it fails can run without review. Anything that costs money or a customer gets a person. Keep most of the volume in the first group and the checking stays small.

Eleven hours a week back, per person, is about 570 hours a year. That is roughly fourteen working weeks. Across a team it is 143 hours a month that did not go into the product, the pitch, the hire or the sleep.

Nobody spends fourteen working weeks on a dashboard. They take the holiday they cancelled twice. They ship the second product that has been a note on a phone for three years. They hire the person they could not train because there were no hours left. They stop dreading Mondays.

sections.h: Count your own hours before you believe any of this
p: The prices here are Twinthos list prices at October 2026: £5,000 a month with a three month minimum, and £999 for the Operations Audit. The wage figures are the official rate and the published survey, both linked below. None of it is a promise that you will save what this page suggests. Count your own hours before and after. That is the only number worth signing against.

table:
| Who is doing the admin | Hours a week | Cost an hour | Cost a year |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| One person, minimum wage | 11 | £13.20 | £7,562 |
| One person, with NI, pension and overhead | 11 | about £17.00 | about £9,745 |
| Two people sharing the load | 11 each | £13.20 | £15,124 |
| Three people sharing the load | 11 each | £13.20 | about £22,700 |
takeaway: The token bill is noise. The monthly fee is the visible cost and the review time is the hidden one. Before you sign, count the hours your team spends on admin in an ordinary month, then count how many of those a system could carry without a person checking each one. That second number is the only saving that is real.

faq.q: Does the £1.60 an hour figure include everything?
faq.a: No. It is the monthly fee spread across the hours the service covers and the work it carries at once. Your own review time and the setup work sit outside it, and those are the lines that decide whether it pays.

faq.q: Where does the eleven hours a week come from?
faq.a: The American Express SME Business Barometer, July 2026, which found UK small business owners and staff spend an estimated 11 hours a week on admin and finance. Secondary reporting agrees on the figure.

faq.q: Is this a promise that we will save money?
faq.a: No. The prices are Twinthos list prices at October 2026 and the wage figures are the official rate and the published survey. The only figure worth trusting is the one you count yourself.
